translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy the brother,
to the holy and faithful brothers in Colossae, in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; we pray for you always.
We have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of your love toward all the saints,
because of the hope prepared for you in the heavens, of which you heard beforehand in the word of the truth of the gospel,
which has reached you, as it has in all the world, and is fruitful and growing, as it is among you also, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
just as you learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,
and who also told us of your love in the Spirit.
For this reason we also, from the day we heard, do not cease praying and asking for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
so that you may walk worthily of God, in all that pleases him, fruitful in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
strengthened with all power according to the might of his glory, for all patience and long-suffering, with joy,
giving thanks to the Father, who has made us worthy of the portion of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
who has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
from whom we have redemption and the forgiveness of our sins.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

For through him was created everything in the heavens and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or lordships, or principalities or authorities: all things were created through him and for him.
He himself is before all things, and all things were established by him.
And he is the head of the body, the church, he who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he himself may be chief in everything;
for it pleased all the fullness to dwell in him,
and through him to reconcile all things to himself, he made peace by the blood of his cross, through him, whether on earth or in the heavens.
And you were once estranged and enemies in your mind, in evil deeds,
but now he has reconciled you by the body of his flesh through death, and has presented you holy, spotless and blameless before him,

if you remain founded and established in the faith, and unmoved from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which has been preached among all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and I fulfill what is lacking of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh [?] for the sake of his body, which is the church,
of which I became a minister by the stewardship of God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
the mystery that was hidden from the ages and from the generations, but has now been revealed to his saints,
to whom God willed to make known what is the richness of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ among you, the hope of glory,
whom we preach, teaching every man and instructing every man in all wisdom, so that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.
For this I also toil and strive according to his working, which works in me with power.
For I want you to know what a great struggle I have for you and for those of Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh,
that their hearts may be comforted, joined together in love, toward all the riches of full assurance of understanding, in knowledge of the mystery of God and the Father, and of Christ,
in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
I say this so that no one may put you to shame with words of excess [?].
for even though I am far away in body, yet in spirit I am with you; I rejoice and see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
As you have learned Christ Jesus the Lord, let us walk in him,
founded and built up on him and made firm by faith, as you learned, abounding in him with thanksgiving.
Beware, let no one be the one who takes you captive through love of wisdom and empty deception, according to the teaching of men, according to the rules of this world and not from Christ,
for in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.
And you are filled in him, who is the head of all rule and authority,
by whom you were also circumcised with the circumcision not made by hand, by the stripping off of the body of the sins of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ.
You were buried with him in baptism, with whom you also rose through faith, by the help of God, who raised him from the dead.
And you also were dead in transgressions and in the uncircumcision of your flesh; he made you alive with him, and he forgave us all transgressions.
And he blotted out for us the handwritten record with its decrees, which was opposed to us, and he took it out of the way and nailed it to the cross.
He stripped off the rulers and authorities and made them a spectacle with boldness, and he exposed them in him.
So let no one judge you by food and drink, or in the matter of a feast, or of a new moon, or of sabbaths,
which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body is Christ's.
Let no one overpower you, if he wishes to do so by humility and the rule of angels, which he has not seen, passing judgment in vain, puffed up by the mind of his flesh,
and not holding fast to the head, from which the whole body, formed and joined together from limbs and joints, grows with the growth of God.
If you died with Christ from the elements of this world, why then, as though living in the world, do you issue commands:
"Do not approach, do not even taste, do not even touch",
which are all for corruption through use, according to the commandment and teaching of men?
These things have, as it were, some word of wisdom, by self-chosen rule and humility and unsparing treatment of the flesh, not by any honor for the satisfying of the flesh.
If you have risen with Christ, seek what is of heaven, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Think on the things of heaven and not on the things of earth.
For you died, and your life is hidden together with Christ with God.
When Christ, our life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.
So put to death your members on earth: fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry,
because of which the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience,
In which you too once walked, when you were living in them.
But now you too put away all of it: wrath, anger, wickedness, blasphemy, and shameful speech from your mouth.
Do not lie to one another; strip off the old man with his deeds
and put on the new man, who is renewed unto knowledge according to the likeness of the image of his Creator,
where there is neither Gentile nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slavery, freedom, but Christ is all in all.
Put on, therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, mercy, forbearance, kindness, humility, gentleness, long-suffering,
bearing with one another and forgiving yourselves, if anyone has a complaint against anyone. Just as Christ forgave you, so you also forgive them.
And over all these things, love, which is the firm bond of perfection,
And let the peace of God be established in your hearts, to which you were indeed called in one body, and be givers of thanks.
And let the word of Christ dwell among you richly in all wisdom; teach and instruct yourselves with psalms and hymns and spiritual praises, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
and whatever you do, in word or in deed, everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
Wives, submit to your own husbands, as is pleasing to the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not be bitter toward them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, so that they may not be grieved.
Slaves, obey in everything your masters according to the flesh, not only before their eyes with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but in simplicity of heart, fearing God.
And whatever you do, do it from the heart, as for the Lord and not as for men.
Know that from the Lord you will receive the reward of your inheritance, for you serve the Lord Christ.
But he who does harm will be repaid for the harm he has done, and there is no partiality.
Masters, give what is just and equal to your slaves; know that you too have a Lord in heaven.
Persevere in prayer, and keep watch in it with thanksgiving.
Pray along with this for us as well, that God may open for us a door of the word, to speak the mysteries of Christ, for which I am in bonds,
so that I may make it known, as I ought to speak.
Conduct yourselves in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the times.
Let your speech always be seasoned with grace as with salt, so that you may know how it befits you to give an answer to each one.
Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister and our fellow slave in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me,
whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that he may learn about you and comfort your hearts,
together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you; he will make known to you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, our fellow captive, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (the son of his father's brother), concerning whom you received a command; if he comes to you, receive him,
And Jesus, who was called Justus, who were of the circumcision; these alone are my helpers for the kingdom of God, who have become a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, greets you; he always labors for you in his prayers, that you may stand firm, perfect and filled with all the will of God.
For I bear witness to him that he has great zeal for you and for those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, and Demas.
Give greetings to the brothers in Laodicea and to Nympha and to the assemblies of their household, house by house.
And when you have read this letter, so act that it may also be read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn may read the one from Laodicea.
And say to Archippus: Take heed to the ministry which you have received from the Lord, that you may fulfill it.
The greeting is by my own hand, Paul's. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
